Commentary.Commentary: Right then, we have had a fantastic start to the series, and if this match is any indication of what's to come, we are certainly in for an exciting series. By his own admission, it may have been closer than they would have liked, but Pat Cummins and his team will be pleased to have crossed the line. Meanwhile, Pakistan fought valiantly with the ball and can take heart from their spirited performance as they aim for a stronger batting display in the next game. The action now shifts to Adelaide, where Australia will look to seal the series, while Pakistan will be eager to bounce back and set up a series decider in Perth. The second ODI, another day-night affair, is scheduled for Friday, November 8, with the first ball at 3.30 am GMT. Join us early for all the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

The captain of Australia, Pat Cummins says that it got a bit tighter than they would have hoped but is happy that they got over the line. Shares that he is happy with the way they bowled. When asked about using eight bowling options, he says that he was trying to keep it interesting and Marnus Labuschagne was always in his ear so he had to have an over. Mentions that they were really good for three-quarters of the game. Feels that when you look to play aggressively, it will not come off always. Ends by saying that there is still room to try and find a couple of partnerships.

Mohammed Rizwan, the skipper of Pakistan says that as a captain he wanted his team to fight hard and is happy about that. Adds that bowling from both teams was great. Thanks the crowd for their support they got and appreciates Haris Rauf for the way he bowled and says they let go of a few chances which cost them the game.

Mitchell Starc is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his brilliance with the ball. He says that it feels good to start the summer off in a positive way. Adds that they were on the hunt for Powerplay wickets and he is glad that he managed to pick up a couple of wickets. Feels that it was a positive effort with the ball but were a little sloppy in the field. States that it was a good wicket and thought that Pakistan were below par. Tells that this is a big summer with a series against India coming up but they still have 5 white-ball games before that.
Time for the presentation ceremony...

Steve Smith is in for a chat and he says Pakistan bowled really well in the middle and they as a team kept charging hard and kept failing. Adds that the wicket was two-paced with a few balls stopping and skidding off the deck with variable bounce which made it hard to bat on. Appreciates Inglis and says he is batting really well and talks about how good he was feeling out there himself and wanted to stay longer. Concludes that Pat Cummins batted exceptionally under pressure and hopes for him to continue throughout the summer.

Earlier in the game, after being asked to bat, Pakistan struggled to find momentum, with several batters getting starts but failing to make it count. Mitchell Starc removed both openers, putting Pakistan on the back foot early. While Babar Azam showed promise, he couldn’t convert it into a big score, and Mohammad Rizwan’s innings was hampered by a lack of rhythm. Pakistan found themselves in deep trouble at 117/6, but Naseem Shah’s entertaining cameo late in the innings pushed them to a somewhat respectable 203, a total that seemed unlikely at one stage. Australia deployed as many as eight bowlers, with Starc standing out for his stellar figures of 3/33 from 10 overs, including three maidens.

However, the game took a dramatic turn when Haris Rauf dismissed Smith, opening the door slightly for Pakistan. Shaheen Afridi then removed Inglis, and Rauf struck twice in two balls, causing Australia to crumble from 139/3 to 139/6. A couple of brain-fade moments from Hardie and Abbott kept Pakistan in the contest, but amidst the chaos, Cummins shone through with a cool-headed finish.

Chasing 204, Australia’s new opening pair of Matthew Short and Jake Fraser-McGurk adopted an aggressive approach but both fell early while attempting to dominate. Pakistan, however, struggled to maintain the pressure after these initial breakthroughs, with their discipline waning at times. Steven Smith looked in sublime touch from the outset, and Josh Inglis, who was given a life on 7 when Irfan Khan dropped a tough chance, grew in confidence as the innings progressed. Together, Smith and Inglis chipped away at the target.

Wow, what a game! A low-scoring thriller to kick off the men’s international cricket summer in Australia! The match was packed with twists and turns, but Australia ultimately prevailed in a nail-biting chase. Credit to Pakistan for battling until the final run, but Australia’s batting depth made the difference, with Pat Cummins staying composed under pressure to guide his team over the line.

OUT! RUN OUT! Oh, dear, that's sloppy from Sean Abbott and this wicket could cost them the game. Shaheen Afridi bangs it into the deck, on a back of a length and on off, Pat Cummins punches it well through cover and gets two runs with ease. Salman Agha charges for the ball, slides ahead and picks it up nicely to throw it. His throw lacks power and it dribbles towards the bowling end. Pat Cummins sets off for the third and so does Sean Abbott. Shaheen Afridi moves across to collect the ball and turns around to hit the bullseye at the striker's end. Sean Abbott wasn't expecting the throw to be relayed back at his end and failed to make his ground in time. The third umpire is called into action and the replays show that Sean is short of his crease. Big, big moment in the game.

Drinks break! Australia have recovered well after the early loss of the two openers. Steven Smith has looked solid as ever and Josh Inglis is slowly but surely growing into confidence. Despite taking a couple of wickets early, Pakistan haven't been able to sustain any substantial pressure on the hosts. Australia have kept the scoreboard ticking at a healthy rate, and unless Pakistan manage to trigger a dramatic collapse, the hosts seem well on track for a comfortable win here.

Commentary.Commentary: Hurls it on a length, on off, a hint of late inward movement, Steven Smith shows the full face of the bat and pushes it to the right of mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Shaheen Afridi to Steven Smith, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: This comes back in off the deck, on a back of a length, on middle, Steven Smith gets on top of it and tucks it right in between the two fielders stationed close at square leg. Smith comes back for the second run with ease.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Shaheen Afridi to Steven Smith, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: This skids off the deck, on a back of a length, on off, Steven Smith goes on the back foot to defend it with a straight bat but gets beaten on the inside edge and wears it high on the back pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Shaheen Afridi to Steven Smith, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: An absolute snorter from Afridi! Bends his back and digs it in short and over middle and leg, the ball kicks off the deck a bit more and Steven Smith is hurried as he looks to stick his bat ahead and keep it out. The ball goes off the shoulder and lands safe on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Shaheen Afridi to Steven Smith, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Josh Inglis walks out to bat at number 4 for Australia!

OUT! TAKEN! Naseem Shah roars in delight! Jake Fraser-McGurk runs out of luck and Pakistan have managed to send both openers back in the hut early. Naseem lands it on a back of a length, on middle and leg, Jake Fraser-McGurk hangs back and shapes up to go across the line. The ball gets big on him and hits the splice of the bat. It balloons towards wide mid on where Irfan Khan takes a dolly.
Commentary.Howout: c Irfan Khan b Naseem Shah
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Naseem Shah to Jake Fraser-McGurk, OUT! c Irfan Khan b Naseem Shah.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on off, Jake Fraser-McGurk looks for a big swing but gets a thick outside edge that flies over backward point for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Naseem Shah to Jake Fraser-McGurk, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Honing in at the pads, on a back of a length, Steven Smith gets on his toes and gets inside the line to nudge it through square leg. Two fielders give it a chas and cut it off. Three runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Naseem Shah to Steven Smith, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Naseem bends his back and digs it in short but this sails over the batter's head for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Naseem Shah to Steven Smith, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: This is on a short of a length, on off, Smith keeps it out on the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Naseem Shah to Steven Smith, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A big mix-up but no harm done! Naseem bangs it on a back of a length, on off, Jake Fraser-McGurk awkwardly pulls it with the ball stopping in the surface. Miscues the pull but it lands safely in the vacant square leg region. JFM wants to come back for the second and is halfway down the track when Smith sends him back. He is struggling to make his ground as Babar fires in a throw towards the bowling end. Luckily for him, the ball plugs a bit in the outfield and pops out, resulting in all the pace coming off the ball and it balloons towards the bowler. This allows JFM to get back in with a dive.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Naseem Shah to Jake Fraser-McGurk, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: In and around the off-stump line, angling in from over the wicket, on a nagging length, at 136.9 kph, Jake Fraser-McGurk punches it to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Naseem Shah to Jake Fraser-McGurk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shaping back into the right-hander, on a hard length, Steven Smith hops and goes deep in his crease to keep it out. End of a successful over for Afridi and Pakistan!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Shaheen Afridi to Steven Smith, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This leaves the batter and it is on the fuller side, Steven Smith makes the leave.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Shaheen Afridi to Steven Smith, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Afridi digs it in short, at the batter, Steven Smith rides the bounce and helps the pull to the left of deep backward square leg. Gets off the mark with a brace.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Shaheen Afridi to Steven Smith, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Attacks the stumps, on a good length does Afridi, Steven Smith covers the line and tucks it across to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Shaheen Afridi to Steven Smith, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Steven Smith walks in at number 3 for Australia!

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! Fine catch by Saim Ayub! Shaheen Afridi gives Pakistan the early breakthrough. Afridi bashes the back of a length, on off, Matthew Short goes for the pull but fails to get on top of the bounce and tries to drag it away on the leg side. Gets a top edge that goes straight up towards backward point. The keeper, the deep third fielder and Saim Ayub from backward point converge with Ayub turning around, trying to settle under it from the mentioned position. He calls for it and takes a safe catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Saim Ayub b Shaheen Afridi
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Shaheen Afridi to Matthew Short, OUT! c Saim Ayub b Shaheen Afridi.

Commentary.Commentary: Not in control but JFM gets away with it! Angling across the batter, near the tramline on off, on a length, Jake Fraser-McGurk stays rooted in the crease and flays at the delivery. Gets a thickish outside edge that flies down to deep third. Collected on the bounce by Naseem in the deep. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Shaheen Afridi to Jake Fraser-McGurk, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A tighter line, on off and middle, on a hard length, Jake Fraser-McGurk dabs it down in front of mid-wicket and gets to the other end quickly. An expensive first over from Naseem. 14 runs off it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Naseem Shah to Jake Fraser-McGurk, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR LEG BYES! A bit too straight from Naseem, on a nagging length, on the pads, Jake Fraser-McGurk tries to help it away but misses. The ball comes off his pads and races down to the deep fine leg fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Naseem Shah to Jake Fraser-McGurk, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Not the cleanest connection but JFM will take it! Fuller and on off, Jake Fraser-McGurk holds his shape and swipes across the line. Gets enough bat on it to clear mid-wicket and picks up a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Naseem Shah to Jake Fraser-McGurk, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! On a back of a length but down leg, Jake Fraser-McGurk swings to heave it away but misses. Wide given.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Naseem Shah to Jake Fraser-McGurk, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Slanting in again, on a length, on middle and leg, Jake Fraser-McGurk chips it up and over wide mid on for a couple of runs more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Naseem Shah to Jake Fraser-McGurk, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling in, on a good length, on off, Jake Fraser-McGurk defends it out solidly.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Naseem Shah to Jake Fraser-McGurk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air...but safe! A real teaser for Babar Azam at mid off. Naseem serves it on a length, on off, Jake Fraser-McGurk looks to go back over the bowler's head but goes through his shot a bit early. Gets more height than distance on it and it goes very high towards mid off. Babar Azam turns around and goes after it. Gives it a good chase but the replays show that he almost overran the ball and it landed over his left shoulder. A couple of runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Naseem Shah to Jake Fraser-McGurk, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: It will be Naseem Shah to share the attack from the other end!

Afridi drags the length back and gets the ball to move back into the right-hander, on a back of a length, Matthew Short sets himself up to heave it away but fails to get any bat on it. The ball goes under his bat and hits him high on the thigh pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Shaheen Afridi to Matthew Short, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angles one across the batter now, on a length, Jake Fraser-McGurk drops it with soft hands in front of cover and takes a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Shaheen Afridi to Jake Fraser-McGurk, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shaheen Afridi goes full in search of swing but gets the line slightly wrong, serves it on the pads, Jake Fraser-McGurk clips it through square leg. Naseem Shah runs and slides to his left from deep backward square leg to mop it up. A couple of runs for JFM to open his account.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Shaheen Afridi to Jake Fraser-McGurk, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Shaping back into the right-hander, on the fuller side, Jake Fraser-McGurk goes deep in his crease and presents a straight bat to push it to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Shaheen Afridi to Jake Fraser-McGurk, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sprayed on the pads, on a length, Matthew Short glances it down to deep backward square leg for a single. Short and Australia are underway!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Shaheen Afridi to Matthew Short, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A hint of inward shape first up for Shaheen as he steams in from over the wicket. Lands it on a good length, on middle and leg, Matthew Short wrists it to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Shaheen Afridi to Matthew Short, No run.
